content.text:
Reviewed all uncommitted changes (60 modified tracked files + ~45 new untracked files, largely a big OpenUI/learner-response/host-execution feature batch) at medium effort: 7 finder angles in parallel, then independent verification on the strongest candidates.

7 findings, most severe first:

1. web/src/components/V240OpenInterfacesArticle.tsx:146 (CONFIRMED) — references an undefined <CodeBlock> component; fails tsc --noEmit and will throw at render when the blog post is visited.
2. web/src/keating/openui/segments.ts:33 (CONFIRMED) — fallback OpenUI doc IDs hash only header+position, not content; two unrelated same-position documents collide and silently share persisted UI state.
3. web/src/keating/openui/segments.ts:61 (CONFIRMED) — the closing-fence regex isn't string-literal-aware (unlike upstream @openuidev/lang-core), so a prop value embedding a markdown code sample truncates the program early.
4. web/src/components/SandboxView.tsx:777 (CONFIRMED) — Stop button now also requires runtime.mode === "browser-nodepod"; if the mode changes while a NodePod is still running (e.g. via runProbe), neither Stop nor Boot renders, leaving the pod un-killable from the UI.
5. web/src/hooks/useKeatingAgent.tsx:448 (PLAUSIBLE) — the new retry-gating logic can silently no-op after an auth error if the message preceding an errored turn isn't user/user-with-attachments/toolResult, versus the old unconditional retry.
6. web/src/lib/sanitize-svg.ts:7 (PLAUSIBLE) — foreignobject removed from the hard element block list; currently latent since no live caller passes untrusted content through it, but it's a real defense-in-depth loss if that changes.
7. web/server/api/agent-runtime/config.ts:58 (CONFIRMED, altitude) — host execution is modeled as a hostProvider flag bolted onto "remote" mode, with the same derivation hand-duplicated in web/src/keating/agent-runtime.ts; the two have already drifted slightly.

Note: one finder agent (simplification angle) hit an API connection error mid-run and its output was unusable — not represented in the results above. A response-comparison.ts candidate ("picks wrong assistant message") was investigated and REFUTED — the alternative session is hidden/read-only until a choice is made, so the scenario isn't reachable.

I’m treating this as a request to remediate the seven findings, preserving the larger uncommitted feature batch and avoiding unrelated cleanup. I’ll first validate each location and its nearby tests/contracts, then patch in small units and run the repo’s focused checks. I’m using the frontend hardening guidance for the UI/runtime cases and the required Vet pass after each logical change.

The hardening guidance requires a quick product-context pass before touching frontend behavior. I’m doing that now, then I’ll map each report to the smallest safe change and identify existing regression-test seams.

content.text: The runtime already has a basic retry wrapper, but it treats several permanent quota failures as transient, recognizes errors mostly by scraping message strings, and loses all retry-attempt context before the UI sees the final failure. The UI also has a separate, narrower classifier, so retry behavior and human guidance can disagree. I’m consolidating those into one failure model first; that gives both automatic recovery and the visible error card the same answer.

The shared classifier now distinguishes transient rate limits/outages from permanent billing, credential, context-window, model, permission, safety, and request-shape failures. It also reads structured status and `Retry-After` data when providers expose it, instead of relying only on error strings. Per the repository workflow, I’m running Vet on this logical unit before wiring it into streaming and UI.
